title: Shortlist a framework from the constraints you can defend
description: Choose the workload, production target, team strength, and artifact contract. Every selection contributes zero to three visible suitability points.
scoringNote: The model intentionally omits performance claims. Run the same representative model, data path, precision, and target hardware before making the decision.

options.label: General model training
options.detail: Standard supervised or generative-model development with established libraries.

options.label: Custom or dynamic research
options.detail: Novel control flow, custom gradients, or rapid model surgery matters.

options.label: Composable scientific transforms
options.detail: Function transformations, explicit vectorization, and accelerator-oriented numerical work matter.

options.label: Python model service
options.detail: The production owner can run a supported Python framework runtime.

options.label: Mobile or embedded device
options.detail: A small target-specific runtime and supported hardware backend are required.

options.label: Accelerator mesh
options.detail: Explicit sharding and multi-device compilation are central constraints.

options.label: PyTorch production experience
options.detail: The team already debugs, profiles, exports, and operates PyTorch workloads.

options.label: TensorFlow production estate
options.detail: Existing pipelines, serving, mobile, and operator ownership use TensorFlow artifacts.

options.label: Functional and compiler expertise
options.detail: The team is comfortable with pure functions, transforms, device meshes, and compiler diagnostics.

options.label: Python runtime is acceptable
options.detail: The production contract may include framework code and a Python process.

options.label: Exported runtime artifact
options.detail: Production requires a versioned artifact with a separately owned runtime.

options.label: Multiple target platforms
options.detail: The model must be validated across server, browser, mobile, or embedded boundaries.

frameworks.label: PyTorch
frameworks.artifactBoundary: Python module for eager execution; torch.export for captured programs; ExecuTorch .pte for supported edge backends.
frameworks.evidence: Strong general ecosystem and eager development path, with separate compile and export contracts that still require target validation.

frameworks.label: TensorFlow
frameworks.artifactBoundary: Keras or SavedModel export for serving and conversion; target-specific TensorFlow Lite artifacts for supported edge runtimes.
frameworks.evidence: Integrated training and deployment formats are useful when the organization already owns their serving and conversion lifecycle.

frameworks.label: JAX
frameworks.artifactBoundary: Transformed JAX program and explicit sharding in Python; exported lowered computation only where the consuming runtime contract is supported.
frameworks.evidence: Composable transformations and explicit accelerator sharding can fit numerical research, but the team must own more of the surrounding production stack.
